newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks surge to year high on merger fever.
newsitem.headline: French stocks surge to year high on merger fever.

text.p: Merger fever and comments on the dollar from a Bundesbank official seen as benign for the franc hustled the bourse to a year high on Tuesday.
Traders said the merger of insurers UAP and Axa spurred the insurance sector and sent bank BNP, a major UAP shareholder, soaring.
UAP and Axa will stay suspended until further notice. BNP welcomed the deal which will create one of the world's biggest insurers.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 23.93 points or 1.09 percent at 2,229.13, while the CAC-40 futures contract was up at 2,243 from 2,210 on Friday's close.
Volume was a hefty 6.3 billion francs.
BNP shot up 8.45 percent to 216.80 francs, while insurer AGF added 3.99 percent to 164.10, on expectations of higher profitability in the face of more competition.
One analyst at a French brokerage thought the UAP-Axa merger was politically inspired, as a means of keeping UAP firmly in French hands.
Axa chairman Claude Bebear called the merger the "deal of the century in French insurance".
French brokerage SGE Delahaye downgrades Suez to neutral from outperform. Suez ends up 0.5 francs at 226.50 francs.

A fund manager said Suez could suffer from the UAP-Axa merger as the insurers and BNP could sell their stakes in the holding company as a non-core asset, which could put 15 percent of Suez capital on the market.
Paribas was among stocks caught up in the merger-induced rally in the financial sector, with the shares climbing 4.26 percent to 343 francs.
Financial stock Cie Bancaire, building on last week's gains, added 2.91 percent to 565 francs amid market talk of major buying from a big French broker.

Bundesbank directorate member Edgar Meister said the current dollar exchange rate was "not appropriate". The dollar rose, which heartened French operators as dollar strength could help U.S. appetite for foreign assets and the franc indirectly benefits from dollar gains against the mark.
